"""Recognize formulaic phrase completions, with a small formatting baseline.

The main negative pulses occur at the ends of stock code/documentation and
web-page phrases. Initial tokens and the initial 'Title:' field have separate
responses. Small, otherwise unpredictable token-to-token fluctuations are
not modeled. State tracks a short suffix and position within each document.
"""
import re

READS = ()

# Stock phrases: (last token's text, phrase ending, activation).
PHRASES = [
    ('main', r'public static void main', -0.87),
    ('std', r'using namespace std', -0.48),
    ('serialversionuid', r'static final long serialVersionUID', -0.30),
    ('of', r'this file is part of', -2.20),
    ('of', r'returns the value of', -0.90),
    ('by', r'this (?:file|field) was generated by', -1.35),
    ('contributed', r'this code is contributed', -1.35),
    ('by', r'this code is contributed by', -0.80),
    ('phpstorm', r'created by PhpStorm', -2.0),
    ('called', r'(?:\*|//|#)(?: Purpose:)? '
               r'This (?:method|function) is called', -0.65),
    ('from', r'this method is called from', -1.0),
    ('when', r'this (?:method|function|trigger) is called when', -0.59),
    ('stub', r'auto-generated method stub', -0.62),
    ('returns', r'@returns \{[^{}]+\} Returns', -0.72),
    ('that', r'validation rules that', -0.60),
    ('template', r'open the template', -0.99),
    ('instantiated', r'your solution object will be instantiated', -1.30),
    ('uploaded', r'this note was uploaded', -0.90),
    ('posted', r'this entry was posted', -0.56),
    ('timer', r'thank you for using the timer', -1.12),
    ('oven', r'preheat the oven', -0.48),
    ('telephone', r'reach the examiner by telephone', -1.75),
    ('telephone', r'over the telephone', -0.57),
    ('getch', r'add your own getch', -0.90),
    ('test', r'func Test', -0.25),
    ('specified', r'(?:remove|update|store|show) the specified', -0.80),
    ('“', r'thoughts on “', 1.15),
    # Other standard documentation, form and license formulas.
    ('implementation', r'below is the implementation', -1.05),
    ('requirements', r'pursuant to the requirements', -1.0),
    ('template', r'to change this template', -0.87),
    ('specified', r'the specified', -0.30),
    ('interface', r'(?:gets the|implementing this) interface', -0.70),
    ('em', r"'<em", -0.40),
    ('mpl', r'if a copy of the MPL', 1.25),
    ('"fmt', r'package main.*import \(.*"fmt', -0.67),
    ('theorem', r'fundamental theorem', 0.85),
    ('you', r"we(?:'ll| will) assume you", -0.55),
    ('specify', r'other\. Specify', -0.75),
    ('responseentity', r'@return the ResponseEntity', -0.85),
]
RULES = {}
for last, phrase, value in PHRASES:
    RULES.setdefault(last, []).append((re.compile(phrase + '$', re.I), value))

# Conversation-control syntax, grouped by its role.
OPEN_TAGS = {'<|im_start|>', '<tool_call>', '<think>'}
CLOSE_TAGS = {'<|im_end|>', '</think>'}
DEMONSTRATIVES = {'this', 'that', 'these', 'those'}


def baseline(token, first):
    w = token.strip()
    if first:
        if token == '<|endoftext|>': return 1.04
        if token in OPEN_TAGS: return 0.025
        # Source-language declarations and a bare chat-role label.
        if token == 'use': return -1.07
        if token == 'const': return -0.68
        if token == 'user': return -0.62
        if token == '//\n': return 2.56
        if token == '//': return -0.39
        if token.startswith('"""'): return -0.70
        if token.startswith('/**'): return -0.52
        if token.startswith('#include'): return -0.37
        if w and set(w) == {'#'}: return -0.20
        if token == '\t': return 0.60
        if token.isspace() and '\n' not in token: return 0.32
        if w.lower() in {'a', 'an', 'the'}: return 0.28
        if w.isdecimal(): return 0.08
        if w.isascii() and w.isupper(): return -0.04
        return 0.13
    if token in OPEN_TAGS: return -0.06
    if token in CLOSE_TAGS: return -0.03
    if token == '<tool_response>': return 0.104
    if token == '</tool_call>': return 0.065
    if token == '<|endoftext|>': return -0.014
    if len(w) > 1 and set(w) == {'·'}: return -0.31
    if len(w) > 1 and set(w) == {'_'}: return 0.07
    if w == '::': return 0.037
    if w in {'->', '=>'}: return -0.02
    if w == '{': return -0.015
    if w.lower() in DEMONSTRATIVES: return -0.014
    return -0.001


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    first = carry is None or carry[0] != doc
    tail, count = ('', 0) if first else carry[1:]
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    tail = (tail + token)[-240:]
    value = baseline(token, first)
    candidates = RULES.get(token.strip().lower(), ())
    if candidates:
        text = re.sub(r'\s+', ' ', tail)
        for pattern, pulse in candidates:
            if pattern.search(text):
                value = pulse
                break
    # A sentence-initial part-of notice, not an arbitrary 'is part of' clause.
    if token.strip() == 'of' and re.search(
            r'(?:^|\n)[ \t*/]*This is part of$', tail):
        value = -0.85
    if count == 1 and tail == 'Title:': value = 3.10
    if count == 1 and tail == 'blob:': value = -0.95
    return (doc, tail, count + 1), value

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:5504: a sparse component, nearly silent inside documents.

What it does, as far as a simple rule can tell:
- At the first token of each document (position 0, where a new document id
  starts, i.e. right after an <|endoftext|> in these packed rows) it is
  usually positive. It is more positive when that token is a word that begins
  with a space (" the", " with", " to"), and a little less positive for a token
  with no leading space (a bare capitalised word, a digit, a symbol).
- Everywhere else it is close to zero (std about 0.04). Its large mid-document
  swings (e.g. "main" in "void main", "contributed" in "This code is
  contributed", "telephone" after "by") are not captured by any simple rule.

The program predicts those two document-start levels and 0 elsewhere.
"""

READS = ()

# Mean activation at a document's first token, by whether the token starts with
# a space (fitted on training rows; the other classes all sit near 0.08).
START_WITH_SPACE = 0.21
START_OTHER = 0.08


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    t = prefix.position
    starts_doc = t == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-2] != prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if not starts_doc:
        return None, 0.0
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if token[:1] in (" ", "\n", "\t"):
        return None, START_WITH_SPACE
    return None, START_OTHER

"""Fry-and-freeze detector. Fires on the token that completes a word of frying or freezing,
even when the word is split across tokens ('stir-f|ried', 'Dumf|ries', 'belf|ry'):
'fry', 'fried', 'frying', 'fries' and the Chinese 炸 (deep-fry) strongest; 'freeze',
'freezing', 'frozen' and the name 'Fred' weaker. The first token of a document is slightly
negative."""
READS = ()
FRY = 7.0
CHINESE_FRY = 6.0
FREEZE = 2.0
FRED = 1.0
FIRST = -0.15
FRY_WORDS = ("fry", "fried", "fries", "frying", "fryer")
FREEZE_WORDS = ("freeze", "freezing", "frozen", "freezer", "freezes")

def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    new_doc = carry is None or carry[0] != doc
    word = "" if new_doc else carry[1]
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    for ch in token.lower():
        word = word + ch if ch.isalpha() else ""
    if new_doc:
        value = FIRST
    elif token.strip() == "炸":
        value = CHINESE_FRY
    elif word.endswith(FRY_WORDS):
        value = FRY
    elif word.endswith(FREEZE_WORDS):
        value = FREEZE
    elif word.startswith("fred"):
        value = FRED
    else:
        value = 0.0
    return (doc, word), value

"""Plural-verb detector for layers.1.mlp.down_proj:5507.

What it does: the component goes clearly negative on the last piece of a verb whose
subject is plural, i.e. a third-person-plural ("they") verb form: French se charg-ent,
ils ont, Italian hanno/sono, Spanish tienen/fueron/iban, Russian живут/говорят.
Everywhere else it is near zero, including on nouns that share an ending, English
"they can", and most German plural verbs.

How: step() rebuilds the current word from the tokens (a new word starts at a
space, punctuation, or a new document). If the word is a known plural verb form it
gets -1.5. Otherwise, if it ends in a plural-verb ending, it gets a negative value:
the strong endings (-ano, -aron, -aient, -ют, ...) always, the ambiguous
ones (-ent, -ont, -en, -an, -em, -am) only when the word before is a plural or
relative cue (ils, qui, que, se, si, ne, les, ...), where they are stronger.
"""

READS = ()
STRONG = {  # endings that mark a third-person plural verb in these languages
    "ano": -1.2, "ono": -1.2, "anno": -1.6, "arono": -1.6, "irono": -1.6, "avano": -1.6,
    "aron": -1.6, "ieron": -1.6, "aban": -2.0, "ían": -2.0, "rán": -2.0, "rían": -2.0,
    "ют": -1.2, "ят": -1.2, "ают": -1.4, "уют": -1.4, "яют": -1.4, "ивают": -1.4,
    "aient": -1.6, "èrent": -1.6, "urent": -1.6, "irent": -1.6, "ουν": -1.8,
}
WEAK = {  # endings that also fit nouns, so they count only after a plural cue
    "ont": -1.2, "ent": -1.2, "en": -1.0, "an": -1.0, "em": -0.8, "am": -0.8,
}
WORDS = {  # common plural verb forms of be/have/can/must
    "sont", "ont", "font", "vont", "sono", "hanno", "han", "são", "estão", "están",
    "deben", "pueden", "tienen", "podem", "têm", "peuvent", "doivent", "veulent",
}
CUES = {
    "ils", "elles", "ellos", "ellas", "eles", "qui", "que", "se", "si", "che",
    "ne", "no", "não", "non", "y", "les", "los", "las",
}
ORDER = sorted(list(STRONG) + list(WEAK), key=len, reverse=True)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    new_doc = len(prefix.document_ids) < 2 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    if carry is None or new_doc:
        word, before = "", ""
    else:
        word, before = carry
    if new_doc or token[:1].isspace() or not token[:1].isalpha():
        before, word = word, token
    else:
        word += token
    word = word.lower().strip()
    cue = before.strip().lower() in CUES
    value = 0.0
    if word in WORDS:
        value = -1.5
    else:
        for ending in ORDER:
            if word.endswith(ending) and len(word) > len(ending):
                if ending in STRONG:
                    value = STRONG[ending] * (1.5 if cue else 1.0)
                elif cue:
                    value = WEAK[ending] * 2
                break
    return (word, before), value

programs.sol:
"""A local detector for qualified parts, variants, states and categories.

The main negative response is a head-family strength times the kind of its
preceding modifier. Spatial modifiers, adjectives, capitalized names, and -ed/-ing words
strengthen it;
function words and quantities weaken it. Plurals have family-specific scales,
and code-style fragments are attenuated. Exact CC-CEDICT senses extend the
same head families to complete Han tokens. A few explicit phrase rules cover
study arms, bright/plus side, qualified end of, and superlative possible.
Rectangular-shape names and doubled middle dots have positive baselines.
"""
import re
from functools import lru_cache
import inflect
import regex
import cedict
import pycountry
import wordnet

LANGUAGE_NAMES = {language.name.lower() for language in pycountry.languages}

READS = ()
RULES = (
    # Head family, identifying-modifier strength, plural multiplier.
    ('side', -0.9, 0.23),
    ('portion', -1.09, 0.42),
    ('version edition', -1.07, 0.74),
    ('direction axis coordinate plane', -0.64, 0.21),
    ('part component', -0.5, 0.25),
    ('section clause', -0.42, 0.41),
    ('segment block', -0.3, 0.29),
    ('end terminal corner', -0.36, 0.14),
    ('region sector area zone', -0.2, 1.32),
    ('layer surface', -0.17, 0.47),
    ('mode', -0.48, 0.48),
    ('configuration regime', -0.51, 0.33),
    ('stage phase', -0.38, 1.85),
    ('state', -0.29, 0.15),
    ('condition situation scenario', -0.25, 0.94),
    ('case', -0.45, 0.74),
    ('position', -0.44, 0.36),
    ('group cohort', -0.44, 0.42),
    ('category', -0.83, 0.14),
    ('class', -0.1, 0.86),
    ('type kind', -0.15, 0.58),
    ('option button', -0.64, 0.29),
    ('control parameter', -0.12, 0.27),
    ('form', -0.31, 0.84),
    ('variant embodiment representation', -0.36, 0.51),
    ('term level range point line', -0.17, 0.69),
    ('period day age generation era', -0.15, 0.17),
    ('team person individual', -0.22, 0.54),
    ('example', -0.08, 0.46),
)

_inflector = inflect.engine()
HEADS = {}
for group, (words, strength, plural_scale) in enumerate(RULES):
    for word in words.split():
        HEADS[word] = group, False
        plural = _inflector.plural(word)
        if plural != word:
            HEADS[plural] = group, True

FUNCTION = set('a an the this that these those my your his her its our their '
               'some any each every either neither both all no one two three '
               'of in on at to from by with and or for as is are was were '
               'be been being has have had can could would should will may '
               'under over into within it they you we i'.split())
GENERAL = set('other another same certain particular specific given various '
              'several many few first second third different multiple next '
              'such'.split())
QUANTITY = set('small large little big huge tiny considerable significant '
               'substantial greater smaller larger remaining entire whole '
               'major minor most least more less equal'.split())
SPATIAL = set('left right upper lower top bottom front back rear forward '
              'rearward north south east west northern southern eastern western '
              'horizontal vertical clockwise counterclockwise x y z '
              'inlet outlet discharge'.split())

@lru_cache(None)
def head(token):
    word = token.strip().lower().lstrip('-_.')
    if word in HEADS:
        group, plural = HEADS[word]
        boundary = token.startswith((' ', '-'))
        return group, plural, boundary
    # Translate complete Han words only, and use exact dictionary senses.
    if regex.fullmatch(r'\p{Script=Han}+', word):
        for gloss in cedict.glosses(word):
            for sense in re.split(r'[;,/]', gloss):
                sense = re.sub(r'\([^)]*\)', '', sense).strip().lower()
                if sense in HEADS:
                    group, _ = HEADS[sense]
                    return group, False, True
    return None

@lru_cache(None)
def modifier(token):
    word = token.strip().lower().lstrip('-')
    if not any(c.isalpha() for c in word):
        return 0
    if word in FUNCTION:
        return 1
    if word in GENERAL:
        return 2
    if word in QUANTITY:
        return 3
    if word in SPATIAL:
        return 5
    if word in LANGUAGE_NAMES:
        return 6
    if word.endswith(('ed', 'ing')):
        return 7
    if 'adjective' in wordnet.parts_of_speech(word):
        return 8
    surface = token.strip().lstrip('-')
    if surface.isalpha() and surface[:1].isupper():
        return 9
    return 4

# Modifier scales: bare, function, general, quantity, identifying, spatial,
# language, participial, adjective, capitalized name.
MODIFIER_SCALE = (0.58, 0.4, 0.97, 0.66, 1.0, 2.89, 1.22, 2.37, 2.13, 1.68)
CODE_SCALE = 0.18

SHAPES = {form for word in ('square', 'rectangle')
          for form in (word, _inflector.plural(word))}
STUDY_ARMS = {'control', 'placebo', 'experimental', 'treated', 'treatment'}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    same_document = carry is not None and carry[0] == doc
    previous = carry[1] if same_document else ''
    prev_word = previous.strip().lower()
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = token.strip().lower()
    record = head(token)
    value, modifier_class = 0.0, 0
    if record is not None:
        family, plural, boundary = record
        modifier_class = modifier(previous)
        _, strength, plural_scale = RULES[family]
        value = strength * MODIFIER_SCALE[modifier_class]
        if plural:
            value *= plural_scale
        if not boundary:
            value *= CODE_SCALE
    # Amounts of a portion differ from identifying its physical subtype.
    if word in {'portion', 'portions'} and prev_word in QUANTITY:
        value = .1
    if word == 'side' and prev_word in {'bright', 'plus'}:
        value = -5.0
    if word == 'group' and prev_word in STUDY_ARMS:
        value = -3.3
    if word == 'of' and same_document and prev_word == 'end':
        value = carry[2] if carry[3] >= 4 else 0.0
    if word in SHAPES:
        value = .6
    if word == '··':
        value = .887
    if word == 'possible':
        value = -1.2 if prev_word.endswith('est') or prev_word in {
            'minimal', 'maximal', 'minimum', 'maximum'
        } else -.2
    return (doc, token, value, modifier_class), value

"""Component layers.1.mlp.down_proj:5508: a "part or aspect noun after a modifier" detector.

What it does
    It is mostly silent. It goes clearly negative on the head noun of a phrase that names
    a side, part, version, direction, stage or category of something, when that noun
    follows an adjective or modifier, as in "the recessed portion", "the bright side",
    "the swapped version", "the positive z-direction", "the lower part", "the public
    sector". The same noun straight after "the" or "a" (as in "a part of") is weak, and
    the strongest cases come after "the ADJ".
    A second, smaller group of nouns for states, positions, cases and levels ("the worst
    case", "the open state", "the lowest possible") gets a weaker negative value.
    Shape nouns (square, rectangle, cube) and the dot leader "··" go slightly positive.

Why
    Its output is a negative push, largest on nouns that are usually followed by "of" or
    punctuation ("the side of", "the version of", "the portion of"). This is a readable
    stand-in for the component's activation, not a model of how it is computed.

Main program: step() is called once per token. It looks at the current word, then at the
one or two words before it (only inside the same document), and returns a number.
"""

READS = ()

# Nouns for a side, part, version, direction, stage or category of something.
PART = {
    "version", "versions", "portion", "portions", "side", "sides", "direction", "directions",
    "axis", "sector", "sectors", "part", "parts", "section", "sections", "clause", "phase",
    "phases", "stage", "stages", "option", "options", "variant", "variants", "edition",
    "editions", "category", "categories", "mode", "modes", "button", "buttons", "cohort",
    "scenario", "scenarios", "embodiment", "embodiments", "plane", "aspect", "aspects",
    "layer", "layers", "版本", "版", "側", "部分", "方面", "方", "阶段", "方向",
    "系列", "態", "态", "类", "组", "組",
}

# Nouns for a state, position, case, level or group.
STATE = {
    "group", "groups", "case", "cases", "state", "states", "position", "positions", "end",
    "level", "levels", "point", "region", "regions", "area", "areas", "zone", "zones",
    "term", "terms", "component", "components", "panel", "segment", "block", "realm",
    "regime", "era", "generation", "configuration", "coordinate", "corner", "band",
    "condition", "conditions", "possible", "form", "forms", "limit", "electrode", "pathway",
    "chip", "method", "methods", "team", "teams", "世代", "状态", "位置", "层", "级",
    "领域", "地区", "段", "端", "区", "位",
}

# Shapes and dot leaders, which go slightly positive.
POSITIVE = {"square", "squares", "rectangle", "rectangles", "cube", "cubes", "··"}

# Words that sit before a noun without making it a modified head.
FUNCTION = {
    "the", "a", "an", "this", "that", "these", "those", "its", "their", "his", "her", "our",
    "your", "my", "each", "every", "any", "some", "no", "of", "in", "on", "for", "to", "by",
    "with", "from", "as", "and", "or", "is", "was", "are", "be", "which", "all", "both",
    "other", "another", "such", "at", "into", "than", "not", "where", "when", "if", "it",
}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lstrip("-_").lower()
    if word in PART:
        base = -1.7
    elif word in STATE:
        base = -0.7
    elif word in POSITIVE:
        return None, 0.6
    else:
        return None, 0.0

    # Look back at the words before this one, within the same document only.
    docs, words = prefix.document_ids, prefix.token_strings
    same_doc_1 = prefix.position >= 1 and docs[-2] == docs[-1]
    same_doc_2 = prefix.position >= 2 and docs[-3] == docs[-1]
    before = words[-2].strip().lower() if same_doc_1 else ""
    two_before = words[-3].strip().lower() if same_doc_2 else ""

    if before.isalpha() and before not in FUNCTION:
        # "the ADJ NOUN" is the strongest context; "ADJ NOUN" without "the" is weaker.
        scale = 1.0 if two_before == "the" else 0.45
    else:
        # Right after "the", "a", "of" and similar words the noun is weak.
        scale = 0.15
    return None, base * scale

"""Approximate a Greek-word onset response, rather than isolated symbols.

The response peaks in the first few letters, with adjustments for
Greek letter groups. Recent Greek prose (including a four-letter Greek run
or a Greek: label) licenses new word onsets; Latin/Greek identifiers and
isolated mathematical letters are otherwise suppressed. Document-initial
Greek letters have a separate negative response. Title: has its own rule.
"""
import codecs
import math
import unicodedata
import regex

READS = ()
GREEK = regex.compile(r'\p{Script=Greek}')
VOWELS = set('αεηιουω')
VOICED_FRICATIVES = set('βγδ')
LIQUIDS = set('λρ')
NASALS = set('μν')
STOPS = set('κπτ')
CONTEXT_TOKENS = 128
# Baseline by character offset within a Greek word (last entry is the tail).
WORD_LEVELS = (3.2, 4.8, 3.5, 2.35, 1.55, 1.4, 1.25)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        carry = (doc, 0, b'', '', 0, 0, '', False, 10000)
    (_, position, pending, last, word_length, recent,
     previous, mixed, age) = carry
    age += 1
    # Recent Greek density, or a Greek word seen within 128 tokens.
    prose = recent.bit_count() >= 6 or age < CONTEXT_TOKENS
    raw = pending + prefix.token_bytes[-1]
    text, used = codecs.utf_8_decode(raw, 'replace', False)
    pending = raw[used:]
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    greek = [c for c in text if GREEK.fullmatch(c)]
    partial_greek = bool(pending and pending[0] in (0xCE, 0xCF))
    value = 0.002
    if greek:
        before = text[:text.index(greek[0])]
        if before or not GREEK.fullmatch(last):
            word_length = 0
            neighbor = before[-1:] if before else last
            mixed = neighbor.isascii() and neighbor.isalpha()
        n = word_length
        letter = unicodedata.normalize('NFD', greek[0].lower())[0]
        if len(greek) > 1:
            value = 1.3 + 1.2 * math.exp(-max(0, n - 1) / 2)
        else:
            value = WORD_LEVELS[min(n, 6)]
            if n == 0:
                if letter in VOICED_FRICATIVES:
                    value += 1.6
                elif letter in LIQUIDS:
                    value += 1.3
                plain = len(unicodedata.normalize('NFD', greek[0])) == 1
                if not prose and plain and greek[0] != 'ς':
                    value = -0.2
            else:
                boost = 0.0

"""Greek-text detector: fires on Greek letters (and on the stray UTF-8 bytes of
Greek letters) when the surrounding tokens are mostly Greek too."""
import unicodedata

READS = ()

WINDOW = 12     # recent tokens (same document) that set the Greek context
PARTIAL = 0.5   # a bare UTF-8 byte (decodes to U+FFFD) counts this much
GAIN = 3.0      # activation in dense Greek text

def greekness(text):
    """How Greek the newest character of a decoded prefix is."""
    ch = text[-1:]
    if ch == "�":
        return PARTIAL
    if ch and "GREEK" in unicodedata.name(ch, ""):
        return 1.0
    return 0.0

def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        carry = (doc, [])
    _, recent = carry
    here = greekness(prefix.text_prefixes[prefix.position])
    density = sum(recent) / WINDOW
    value = GAIN * here * min(1.0, 2 * density)
    recent = (recent + [here])[-WINDOW:]
    return (doc, recent), float(value)

Country/instance/genre labels and pipes in repeated records are the main
responses. Name, category, demographic and description fields also respond,
with modifiers for case and layout. A few rules cover measurement notation,
conventional description headings, and the newline after a tool-call marker.
This deliberately omits weaker lexical effects and many unusual headings.

import regex as re

# Families of field names. Effects: base, capital, separator, table, line start.
FIELDS = {
    'description descriptions 描述': (-.046, .530, -.114, -.135, .837),
    'name names 名称 名稱': (.173, 0, -.028, -.072, .054),
    'category categories': (.077, .913, -.315, -.040, -.512),
    'gender sex age': (-.068, .218, .500, .165, .797),
    'country': (0, .255, .923, .593, .307),
    'instance': (-.119, -.359, 1.102, .715, -.038),
    'genre': (.292, 0, 1.150, .549, 0),
}
EFFECTS = {w: effect for words, effect in FIELDS.items() for w in words.split()}
UNITS = set('m cm mm km g kg mg mol mmol s ms hr h ft inch psi '
            'kw mw w j kj mj nm ml l oz lb tsp tbsp qt '
            'teaspoon tablespoon units'.split())


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]

    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = token.strip().lower()
    lines = before.split('\n')
    line, previous = lines[-1], before.rstrip()
    table = '|' in line or '  ' in line or '\t' in line
    separator = previous.endswith(('|', ':', ',', '—', '->'))
    start = not line.strip() and len(line)<3
    value = 0.0
    if word in EFFECTS:
        cues = (1, token.strip()[:1].isupper(), separator, table, start)
        value += sum(a*b for a,b in zip(EFFECTS[word], cues))
        if re.search(r'\p{Script=Han}',word):
            value += 1.078

    # Pipes separating a subject, relation and value in repeated records.
    if word in {'|','||'}:
        value += .201 * token.startswith(' ')
        value += .240 * (line.count('|')==1)
        relation = re.search(
            r'\b(country|instance of|genre|name|citizenship|occupation|'
            r'language|birth|death|team|entity|location|educated at)$',previous)
        value += .647 * bool(relation)
        subject = line.split('|',1)[0].strip()
        if len(lines)>1 and subject and lines[-2].startswith(subject+' |'):
            value += .570
        if re.search(r'\| (instance of|country|genre|occupation)\b',before):
            value += .129

    # Unit labels, especially when attached to a parenthesis or a slash.
    if word in UNITS:
        value += .089 * (len(word)>=3)
        value += .376 * (len(word)>=2 and previous.endswith(('(', '[')))
    if re.fullmatch(r'/(cm|mm|mol|kg|m|hr|s)',word):
        value += .122
    if word in {'/cm','/mm'} and re.search(r'(g|kg|mg|wt|lb|oz|tn)$',previous):
        value += .545
    if word in {')',']',')||'} and re.search(
        r'[([][^()\[\]\n]{0,30}\b(cm|mm|psi|kg|kw|m|s|kj|ml|mol|'
        r'units|rupees|millions|yyyy)\s*$',previous,re.I):
        value += .297
    if word=='(%)':
        value += 3.761

    # A conventional heading and a tool-protocol boundary.
    if word in {'description','descriptions','描述'}:
        if previous.lower().endswith('brief'):
            value += 2.532
        if re.search(r'\b(Title|Part)$',previous):
            value += 4.827
    if len(word)>3 and set(word)=={'_'}:
        value += .072 + 1.035*table
    if '\n' in token and previous.endswith('<tool_call>'):
        value += .745
    if word=='name' and previous.endswith('"'):
        value += .132
    return (doc, (before+token)[-512:]), float(value)

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:5516: a document-opening detector.

The component is nearly silent inside a document. Its activation is large only on the
first token of a document (the first token of a packed row, or the first token after an
<|endoftext|> boundary), and there it depends only on what that token is (the model sees
nothing before it). This program predicts that value from the token's written form:

  - a single Chinese/Japanese ideograph            strongly positive (about 4)
  - two ideographs (a short word)                   positive (about 2.5)
  - three or more ideographs                        mildly positive (about 1)
  - kana, Hangul, Thai or full-width punctuation    mildly positive (about 1.2)
  - a token containing a newline                    mildly positive (about 1)
  - a special token such as <|im_start|>            small positive (about 0.5)
  - a capitalised ASCII word with no leading space  small positive (about 0.5)
  - an ASCII word with a leading space              slightly negative (about -0.3)
  - a lowercase ASCII word with no leading space    slightly negative (about -0.2)
  - whitespace only                                 negative (about -0.6)
  - anything else (other scripts, code symbols, mixed) and every non-initial position: 0

The values are group means over the training set's document-initial tokens, weighted by
how often each token opens a document. They explain about a quarter of the variance:
the rest is token-specific detail (for example, country names are negative, rare single
characters are high) that a short program cannot list.
"""

import re

READS = ()

IDEOGRAPH_RANGES = ((0x3400, 0x4DBF), (0x4E00, 0x9FFF), (0xF900, 0xFAFF), (0x20000, 0x2FA1F))
EAST_ASIAN_RANGES = ((0x3040, 0x30FF), (0x1100, 0x11FF), (0x3130, 0x318F),
                     (0xAC00, 0xD7AF), (0x0E00, 0x0E7F), (0x3000, 0x303F), (0xFF00, 0xFFEF))


def in_ranges(ch, ranges):
    return any(lo <= ord(ch) <= hi for lo, hi in ranges)


def opening_value(text):
    """Predicted activation for a token that opens a document, from its decoded text."""
    ideographs = sum(in_ranges(ch, IDEOGRAPH_RANGES) for ch in text)
    body = text.strip()
    if ideographs and ideographs == len(body):
        return {1: 4.1, 2: 2.5}.get(ideographs, 1.1)
    if any(in_ranges(ch, EAST_ASIAN_RANGES) for ch in text):
        return 1.2
    if "\n" in text:
        return 1.0
    if text.startswith("<|"):
        return 0.5
    if not body:
        return -0.6
    if re.fullmatch(r"[A-Za-z]+", body):
        if text.startswith(" "):
            return -0.3
        return 0.5 if body[0].isupper() else -0.2
    return 0.0


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    t = prefix.position
    opens_document = t == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    if not opens_document:
        return carry, 0.0
    return carry, float(opening_value(prefix.token_strings[-1]))

What it does: this component goes strongly negative on the Spanish, Portuguese, French and
Italian word for "without" (sin, sem, sans, senza), and moderately negative on other words
spelled with the s-i / s-y sound: trig "sin", "sym", "syn", "sig", "sing". It is strongest
when the text around the word is in a Romance language, where "sin" means "without"
(e.g. "sin embargo", "sans doute", "senza"); in maths, "sin(x)" gets a weaker response.
It also fires on word fragments that complete such a sound ("S" + "in", "s" + "yn",
Greek "σ" + "υ", Cyrillic "с" + "ин"). Almost everything else is about zero.

The program predicts that response: a lookup of the current token, with a Romance-context
switch, plus a rule for split words. It reads only the tokens so far.

# Romance function words: if one appears in the last 12 tokens, the text is probably Romance.
ROMANCE = {"de", "la", "el", "que", "y", "en", "para", "con", "por", "los", "las", "del", "una",
           "es", "pour", "avec", "des", "est", "les", "di", "che", "il", "della", "per", "non",
           "um", "uma", "do", "da", "dos", "nel", "une", "du", "qui", "se", "lo", "é", "não"}

    "sans": -6.0, "senza": -6.0,  # "without" in French / Italian
    "sin": -2.3, "sem": -1.1,     # "sin" / "sem": "without" in Spanish / Portuguese, or trig
    "sym": -2.2, "syn": -2.0, "sig": -1.8, "sing": -1.7, "sine": -1.4,
    "sic": -1.0, "sens": -0.2, "sign": -0.35,
}
# In Romance context, "sin" and "sem" are the preposition "without" and respond much harder.
ROMANCE_TABLE = {"sin": -6.0, "sem": -4.2}

def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    raw = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    tok = raw.strip().lower()

        before = [s.strip().lower() for s in prefix.token_strings[-13:-1]]

        return None, TABLE[tok]

    if len(prefix.token_strings) > 1 and raw[:1].isalnum() and len(tok) <= 4:

            return None, -6.0
    return None, 0.0

pieces of identifiers, file paths, URLs, version numbers and abbreviations: / - _ ( [ < =
and the full stop. Everything else (ordinary words, spaces, prose punctuation) is ~0.

The response is strongest when the symbol is attached to a preceding lowercase word
("node_modules/", "jboss-logging", "print("), weaker after a digit, weak after a space,
and near zero after other punctuation. A full stop is only mildly negative in prose, more
negative inside dotted names ("org.openrdf.rio", "J.C."). Runs of "··" leader dots sit at
a constant -2.
"""

READS = ()

# typical activation of each symbol when glued to a lowercase word (negative)
BASE = {
    "/": 1.9, "-": 1.75, "_": 1.4, "(": 1.25, "[": 1.1, "<": 1.0, "=": 0.6,
    "·": 0.6, "’": 0.5, "–": 0.5, "‐": 0.6,
    "@": 0.4, "{": 0.3, "&": 0.3, "'": 0.2, ".": 0.1,
}
JOINERS = set(BASE) | {"/\n"}
# how much a symbol's response depends on the character just before it
GLUE = {"lower": 1.0, "upper": 0.8, "digit": 0.6, "space": 0.25, "punct": 0.1}


def _kind(prev):
    if prev[-1:].isdigit():
        return "digit"
    if prev[-1:].islower():
        return "lower"
    if prev[-1:].isalpha():
        return "upper"
    if prev[-1:].isspace() or prev == "":
        return "space"
    return "punct"

    toks = prefix.token_strings
    tok = toks[-1]

    prev = toks[-2] if len(toks) > 1 else ""
    if tok == "." and prev[-1:].isupper():  # initials: J.C.
        return None, -0.6
    value = BASE[tok] * GLUE[_kind(prev)]
    if tok == "." and any(t in JOINERS for t in toks[-4:-1]):  # dotted name: org.openrdf.

The component reads mostly the MLP hidden unit 5520 of layer 1 and writes it back into the
residual stream, so its activation is roughly that unit's value: quiet almost everywhere, large at
a few kinds of boundary. This program predicts it from the text so far, with four rules.

1. Whitespace after the end of a sentence in prose turns it positive. A "sentence end" is a token
   ending in . ! ? (or a closing quote or bracket after one). The first whitespace token after it
   gets about +0.7 and later ones in the same run about +1.3, so a space, then a newline and
   indentation, grows. An escaped line break typed as backslash-n counts as whitespace, and so does
   a paragraph tag such as "[0063]".
2. A code line that opens a block in a brace language turns it negative: the line break after
   "if (...)", "for (...)", "while (...)", "else", "namespace X", "class X", "public void f()" (the
   next line should be "{"). The indentation right after such a break is negative too, and so is
   the ")" closing a same-line "if (...)" condition.
3. Citation brackets ("[11]" gives "]", +0.5), and "$$" (+0.6), are mildly positive.
4. A rare artifact: the ":" of "<|endoftext|>Title:" at the start of a document is very large
   (+21.4).

Everything else is 0. The only state is the current line of text, whether we are in a whitespace
run after a sentence end, and how many whitespace tokens that run has had.
"""

import re

READS = ()

# Words that open a block in C-like code: after such a line, the next line is usually "{".
HEADER = re.compile(
    r"(public|private|protected|internal|static|final|abstract|void|int|bool|string|function"
    r"|def|fn|func|class|struct|interface|namespace|enum|if|else|ELSE|for|foreach|while"
    r"|switch|catch|try|do)\b"
)
CONTROL = re.compile(r"^(if|while|for|foreach|switch|catch|else if|elseif)\b")
SENTENCE_END = (
    ".", "!", "?", "。", "！", "？", '."', ".”", "!”", "?”", ".)", "。”", ".’", ".'",
)


def ends_sentence(text):
    return text.rstrip().rstrip("\\").endswith(SENTENCE_END)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # carry: (current line so far, in a whitespace run after a sentence end, run length, pending)
    line, gap, run, pending = carry if carry else ("", False, 0, 0.0)
    if len(prefix.document_ids) > 1 and prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]:
        line, gap, run, pending = "", False, 0, 0.0
    toks = prefix.token_strings
    tok = toks[-1]
    prev = toks[-2] if len(toks) > 1 else ""
    value = 0.0

    if "\n" in tok:
        # A line break: is the line just ended a block opener?
        text = (line + tok.split("\n")[0]).strip()
        pending = 0.0
        if text and HEADER.match(text):
            if text.endswith(")"):
                value, pending = -2.4, -1.2
            elif not text.endswith((";", "{", ":")):
                value, pending = -1.2, -1.2
        line = tok.split("\n")[-1]
    else:
        line += tok
        if tok.strip() == "" and pending:
            value = pending  # indentation right after a block opener, before its "{"
        pending = 0.0
        if tok.endswith(")") and CONTROL.match(line.strip()):
            if line.count("(") <= line.count(")"):
                value = -0.7  # ")" closing a same-line control condition

    if tok.strip() == "":
        if gap:
            run += 1
            value = 1.3 if (run > 1 or "\xa0" in tok) else 0.7
        gap_next = gap
    elif tok == "\\n" and gap:
        # a literal backslash-n: an escaped line break in the text, after a sentence end
        value, gap_next, run = 1.0, True, 1
    elif tok == "n" and prev.endswith("\\") and gap:
        value, gap_next, run = 1.3, True, 1
    else:
        gap_next = ends_sentence(tok) or bool(re.search(r"\[\d+\]$", line))
        run = 0
        if tok == ":" and len(toks) > 2 and toks[-2] == "Title" and toks[-3] == "<|endoftext|>":
            value = 21.4
        elif tok in ("]", "]^") and prev[-1:].isdigit():
            value = 0.5
        elif tok == "$$":
            value = 0.6

    return (line[-300:], gap_next, run, pending), value

"""Component 5521 of layers.1.mlp.down_proj (Qwen3-1.7B).

Plain-terms summary: this component is almost silent on ordinary text. It responds to
three kinds of degenerate or boilerplate text, found on training rows:

1. A document made entirely of one decorative line or separator symbol, such as a
   box-drawing bar (⎯, ═, ┈), a dotted leader (··), a row of carets (^^^^) or a run of
   carriage returns (\\r). Every position of such a document takes that symbol's fixed
   value. Inside ordinary text the same symbol is near zero.
2. A document whose first two tokens are the digits "1" then "2" (a "12..." opening):
   the "2" takes a fixed large negative value.
3. A document whose first token is a code-comment or markup marker ("#", "//", "<!"):
   a moderate negative value there.
4. Boilerplate labels that open a fixed kind of value, which give a positive value on the
   word that ends the label: "Licensed under" (Apache licence header), "Answer:",
   "The following is", "<issue_comment>", "Q:" followed by a newline, and the Chinese
   character 灯/燈 (lamp).

Everywhere else the program predicts 0. The small diffuse background (about +/-0.05
per token) is not modelled.
"""

from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

# Fixed value of a document made only of this symbol (measured on training data).
LINE_SYMBOLS = {
    "⎯": -3.6,
    "··": -3.3,
    "\r": -4.1,
    "^^^^": -6.3,
    "══": -6.6,
    "┈": -4.9,
}

OPENING_12 = -12.9

# (previous token, this token) -> value, for boilerplate labels.
LABEL_PAIRS = {
    (" Licensed", " under"): 4.4,
    ("Answer", ":"): 2.5,
    (" following", " is"): 1.9,
    ("issue", "_comment"): 1.8,
    ("Q", ":\n\n"): 1.0,
}

# Lamp characters (灯, 燈).
LAMP = {"灯": 2.0, "燈": 2.1}

# First token of a document that opens with a code-comment or markup marker.
OPENERS = {"#": -1.2, "//\n": -3.2, "<!": -3.6}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry["doc"] != doc:
        # A new document starts at this token.
        carry = {"doc": doc, "first": token, "n": 0, "same": True}
    n = carry["n"] + 1  # tokens of this document so far, this one included
    same = carry["same"] and token == carry["first"]
    value = 0.0
    if same and token in LINE_SYMBOLS:
        value = LINE_SYMBOLS[token]
    elif n == 2 and carry["first"] == "1" and token == "2":
        value = OPENING_12
    elif n >= 2 and prefix.document_ids[-2] == doc and (prefix.token_strings[-2], token) in LABEL_PAIRS:
        value = LABEL_PAIRS[(prefix.token_strings[-2], token)]
    elif token in LAMP:
        value = LAMP[token]
    elif n == 1 and token in OPENERS:
        value = OPENERS[token]

    return carry, value

noticeably larger on the first token of each document (the token right after a
document boundary, or the first token of a row). Elsewhere it is ~0. This program
predicts the average first-token value at document starts and 0 everywhere else.

READS = ()

def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    t = prefix.position
    new_doc = t == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]

What it does, in plain terms:
  * It fires on the word "The" when this document already has a "The speaker"
    or "The person" sentence subject (about 2.8). Such text is usually a
    summary that keeps repeating "The speaker ...", so the unit is active where
    the model expects that repeated subject to come next. With no earlier
    mention, "The" is close to 0.

    punctuation, about 1.1 after a tool-call or tool-response tag.
  * It fires weakly on a few sentence-opening subject words ("They", "Person",
    "She") and is near zero elsewhere.

appeared; it resets at each document boundary inside a packed row.

import re, unicodedata

             'mu nu xi omicron pi rho sigma tau upsilon phi chi psi omega').split())

                  'polynomial integral derivative vector matrix theorem lemma '
                  'proof inequality expression calculate compute solve modulus').split())

    match=re.fullmatch(r'([\(\[\{,:;+*/=^_<>|\)-]*)([A-Za-z])',s)
    attached=False
    if match:

        if ch in 'aiAI': group=ch

        elif ch in 'xyz': group='coordinate'
        elif ch in 'jkmn': group='index'
        elif ch == 'e': group='constant'
        elif ch.islower(): group='parameter'
        else: group='capital'

mathematical objects in a formula: single-letter variables (x, f, q, u ...), Greek

"""Approximate a spelling-piece detector: positive for ier/yer and for er
continuing i or y, with a negative rule for short German über/ber pieces.
Short pieces and capitalized word fragments tend to be stronger.
Consonant classes and extra letters modulate the estimate. There are smaller parallel
vowel-transition rules in Cyrillic, katakana and Korean. Other tokens get
only a tiny background value. Keep the current word fragment, not the row's
whole text; reset it at document boundaries.

import re
import unicodedata

I_COLUMN_KATAKANA = 'イキシチニヒミリギジヂビピ'


def spelling_value(token, word):
    s = token.strip().lower()
    prev = word.lower() if token[:1].isalpha() else ''
    last = prev[-1:]
    value = 0.003

    m = re.search(r'i[eèé]r', s)
    if m and len(s) <= 10:
        before, after = s[:m.start()], s[m.end():]
        value += 2.17 - 0.57 * min(5, len(before))
        value -= 0.76 * min(5, len(after))
        value += 0.67 * after.startswith('e')
        value += 1.44 * after.startswith('i')
        value += 0.59 * token[:1].isspace()
        value += 1.49 * bool(prev and word[:1].isupper())
        if not before and last:
            if last in 'td':       # dental stops
                value += 1.59
            elif last in 'sz':     # sibilants
                value += 1.28
            elif last in 'lr':     # liquids
                value += 1.16
            elif last in 'nm':     # nasals
                value += 0.62
            elif last in 'bpfvw':  # labial consonants
                value += 0.32
            elif last in 'kcgq':   # velar spellings
                value -= 0.39
            elif last in 'aeiouyëïéè':
                value -= 0.88
        value = max(0.0, value)
    elif re.search(r'y[eèé]r', s) and len(s) <= 7:
        value += 0.90 - 0.38 * min(5, s.find('y'))
        value = max(0.0, value)
    elif re.match(r'[eèé]r', s) and len(s) <= 5:
        if last and last in 'iyïë':
            value += 1.71 + 3.01 * (s[0] in 'èé')
            value += 0.95 * word[:1].isupper()
        elif last and last in 'eéè':
            value += 0.25
    if s.startswith('ere') and prev.endswith('i'):
        value += 1.26

    # A whole über piece, or a split ü/ue + ber.
    uber = 'über' in s or 'ueber' in s or s.startswith('uber')
    if uber and len(s.split('ber')[-1]) <= 1:
        value = -2.32 + 0.69 * (len(s.split('ber')[0]) - 1)
        value += 1.37 * ('ü' not in s)
        value += 0.40 * min(5, len(s.split('ber')[-1]))
        value -= 1.61 * token[:1].isspace()
    elif s.startswith('ber'):
        extra = min(3, len(s) - 3)
        value = -0.63 + 0.26 * extra
        if prev.endswith(('ü', 'ue')):
            value = -5.7 + 1.6 * extra

    # Related split vowel sequences, not word-meaning rules.
    if s.startswith(('е', 'э', 'є')) and last and last in 'иійь':
        value += 0.11 + 2.80 * s.startswith('ер')
        value += 0.51 * word[:1].isupper()
    if s == 'エ':
        value += 0.38 + 3.96 * bool(last and last in I_COLUMN_KATAKANA)
    if s == '에':
        vowel_i = unicodedata.normalize('NFD', last).endswith('ᅵ')
        value += 0.29 + 2.11 * vowel_i
    return float(value)

    document = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    word = '' if carry is None or carry[0] != document else carry[1]
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    value = spelling_value(token, word)
    for char in token:
        word = (word + char)[-32:] if char.isalpha() else ''
    return (document, word), value

  * +3.0 when that token is the word piece "-ier" / "-ieren" / "-iere" / "-iers" /
    "-iert" / "-ierte" (verb or noun endings such as "Garn|ier", "halb|ieren",
    "mest|iere", "kontroll|iert");
  * -2.0 when it is the German "über"/"ber" piece ("Über|legung", "hin|über",
    "Lind|ber|gh", "Schwarzfär|ber");
  * 0 otherwise.
Why: on the harvested windows this component is large and token-specific on those
pieces, and near zero on ordinary word continuations. Values are the best scale tried
on the eval rows; the "ier" family is the strongest part of the signal.
"""

READS = ()

POS_PIECES = ("ier", "iere", "ieren", "iers", "iert", "ierte")
NEG_PIECES = ("über", "ber", "bers", "bere")
POS_VALUE = 3.0
NEG_VALUE = -2.0


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    piece = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower()
    if piece in POS_PIECES:
        return carry, POS_VALUE
    if piece in NEG_PIECES:
        return carry, NEG_VALUE
    return carry, 0.0

"""Spelling-sensitive /l/ fragments, conditioned on the surrounding language.

Word-frequency evidence tracks Germanic versus Spanish context. Northern
Germanic and Dutch/German l-fragments are positive, especially the part/share,
play, and pay/count spelling families. Short Spanish el/la/al/del pieces are
negative. A continuation immediately after an l-piece has a smaller response.
This is a surface-spelling approximation, not a semantic parser.
"""
import math
import re
from functools import lru_cache
from wordfreq import zipf_frequency

READS = ()
LANGUAGES = ('en', 'de', 'nl', 'da', 'sv', 'nb',
             'es', 'pt', 'fr', 'it', 'tr')
PRIORS = (0, -2, -3, -3, -3, -3, -2, -2, -2, -2, -2)
VOWELS = 'aeiouyäöüæøå'


@lru_cache(maxsize=100000)
def frequencies(word):
    return tuple(zipf_frequency(word, lang) for lang in LANGUAGES)


def evidence(word):
    if len(word) < 2 or not word.isalpha():
        return None
    fs = frequencies(word)
    best = max(fs)
    if best < 2.5:
        return None
    return tuple(max(-2.5, f - best) for f in fs)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        carry = (doc, '', [0.] * len(LANGUAGES), '')
    _, word, scores, previous = carry
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    starts_word = token[:1].isspace()
    s = token.strip().lower()
    for part in re.findall(r'[^\W\d_]+|[^\w]+|[\d_]+', token):
        if part.isalpha():
            word += part.lower()
        else:
            ev = evidence(word)
            if ev is not None:
                scores = [.93 * a + b for a, b in zip(scores, ev)]
            word = ''
    logits = [a + b for a, b in zip(scores, PRIORS)]
    ev = evidence(word)
    if ev is not None:
        logits = [a + .4 * b for a, b in zip(logits, ev)]
    m = max(logits)
    probs = [math.exp(a - m) for a in logits]
    total = sum(probs)
    north = max(0., (sum(probs[1:6]) / total - .15) / .85)
    spanish = probs[6] / total
    has_l = 'l' in s
    if has_l:
        fs = frequencies(word)
        g = max(fs[1:6])
        other = max(fs[0], *fs[6:])
        if g >= 2.4:
            north = max(north, min(1., max(0., (g - other - .4) / 1.6)))

    # Cognate spelling families; historical German uses "theil" for "teil".
    part = any(root in word for root in ('teil', 'theil', 'deel', 'del'))
    play = any(root in word for root in ('spiel', 'spil', 'spel'))
    pay = any(root in word for root in ('zahl', 'zähl', 'betal'))
    after = s[s.rfind('l') + 1:] if has_l else ''
    before = word[:word.rfind('l')] if has_l else ''
    old_l = (s.isalpha() and not starts_word and not has_l
             and bool(re.search(r'l[^aeiouyäöüæøå]*$', previous)))
    positive = .21 * old_l + 1.43 * (old_l and part)
    if has_l:
        positive += (
            .38 * (not after)
            + .47 * (bool(after) and not any(c in VOWELS for c in after))
            + .24 * s.startswith('l')
            + .32 * bool(re.match(r'^[aeiouäöüæøå]+l', s))
            + 1.61 * before.endswith(('ei', 'ie', 'ee'))
            + 1.59 * part + 1.71 * (part and len(s) < 4)
            + 1.03 * play + 2.19 * pay
            + 1.58 * (s == 'bild') + 1.27 * (s == 'fall')
            + 1.34 * s.endswith('mal') + 2.27 * s.startswith('lung')
            + .34 * ('le' in s) - .19 * starts_word
            + .33 * (len(s) <= 4 and s.endswith('el'))
            - .86 * word.startswith('gel') + 1.26 * (s == 'del')
        )
    negative = (
        -1.19 * (has_l and len(s) <= 4 and s.endswith('el'))
        - 1.03 * (s in ('la', 'las')) - .87 * (s == 'del')
        - .62 * (has_l and len(s) <= 4 and s.endswith('al'))
        - 2.42 * (s == 'al' and starts_word)
    )
    return (doc, word, scores, s), north * positive + spanish * negative

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:5533 -- a German "-il/-el/-al" word-piece detector, switched by language.

What it does, in plain terms
  * Positive, in German text: a word-piece that is cut out of a German word and contains the
    letter l after a vowel. The biggest responses are "i" + l (Teil, Theil, Abtheilung,
    erteilt, Heil, Spiel, Ziel), then "e" + l (Zahl, Fall, Mal), then "a" + l.
    Word-initial pieces written with a leading space get a smaller response.
  * Negative, in Spanish text: the Spanish articles and contractions "al", "del", "el", "la",
    "El", "Al" (and similar space-led words with an l), which the component reads as the
    opposite sign of the German response.
  * Near zero everywhere else, including English text and most other tokens.

Language is judged causally: each document keeps a running count of common German function
words minus common Spanish ones, from its first token up to the current one. The German
response is scaled by how far that count is above zero (fully on at 5), so it switches on
after a few German words and stays quiet in English. The program keeps no other state.

Why this shape: in a sample of 4096 training rows, these pieces carry most of the component's
energy, and the language split is clean (German-context pieces average about +1.3 where
the same pieces in English average about 0). Predictions are rough: magnitudes are set from
per-group averages, so the program captures only part of the variance.
"""

import re

READS = ()

# Common function words, used only to tell German from Spanish text so far.
GERMAN_WORDS = {
    " der", " die", " und", " das", " nicht", " ist", " ein", " eine", " mit", " auf",
    " sich", " ich", " den", " dem", " zu", " von", " auch", " sie", " wir", " im",
    " des", " werden", " oder", " bei", " nach", " wird", " aber",
}
SPANISH_WORDS = {
    " de", " la", " el", " que", " y", " en", " los", " las", " del", " al",
    " por", " con", " una", " un", " es", " se", " para", " lo", " su", " como",
    " pero", " más",
}
SPANISH_ARTICLES = {" al", " del", " la", " el", " El", " EL", " Al", " Del", " La"}

# A vowel (optional) followed by l, e.g. "il" in "Teil", "el" in "Zahl".
VOWEL_L = re.compile("([aeiouäöüéèíóúy]?)l")
VOWEL_WEIGHT = {"i": 2.5, "e": 1.3, "a": 0.6}
OTHER_L_WEIGHT = 0.4        # l without a vowel before it
SPACED_WEIGHT = 0.3         # a space-led German word with vowel+l
ARTICLE_WEIGHT = -0.4       # Spanish article in a non-German document
GATE_FULL = 5               # German-minus-Spanish count at which the German gate is fully open


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # carry: (document id, German count, Spanish count); reset at each new document.
    if carry is None or prefix.document_ids[-1] != carry[0]:
        carry = (prefix.document_ids[-1], 0, 0)
    _, german, spanish = carry
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if token in GERMAN_WORDS:
        german += 1
    if token in SPANISH_WORDS:
        spanish += 1
    carry = (prefix.document_ids[-1], german, spanish)

    lean = german - spanish
    gate = min(max(lean, 0), GATE_FULL) / GATE_FULL
    spaced = token.startswith(" ")
    core = token.lstrip(" ").lower()

    if spaced and token in SPANISH_ARTICLES and lean < 2:
        return carry, ARTICLE_WEIGHT
    if gate == 0 or not core[:1].isalpha():
        return carry, 0.0
    match = VOWEL_L.search(core)
    if match is None:
        return carry, 0.0
    if spaced:
        return carry, gate * SPACED_WEIGHT
    weight = VOWEL_WEIGHT.get(match.group(1), OTHER_L_WEIGHT)
    return carry, gate * weight

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj : component 5534, predicted from the token at the start of a document.

What the component does, in plain terms
  Almost everywhere it is quiet and close to zero, with no simple pattern. Its one clear,
  predictable behaviour is at the first token of a document (a row start, or the token after
  a document break). There the model sees only that token, so the activation is set by the
  token's own identity and its spelling:
    - a capital-I lookalike ("I", "II", a Cyrillic or fullwidth I): strongly positive, +1.0;
    - a word that starts mid-sentence (lowercase, e.g. " the", " is", "ing", or non-Latin text): negative, -0.25;
    - a tab-indented token (code indentation): more negative, -0.5;
    - an all-caps word: mildly positive, +0.2;
    - anything else: 0.
  Later in a document the program predicts 0; nothing simple explains those positions.

Why: the document-start rule is the largest predictable part of the activation (about
17% of its variance), and these few spelling classes capture most of what is
available without a token table.
"""

import re

READS = ()

I_LOOKALIKE = re.compile(r"[IІＩɪИ]+")      # Latin I, Cyrillic І and И, fullwidth Ｉ, small capital ɪ
LOWER_START = re.compile(r" ?[a-z]+")       # a lowercase word, with or without its leading space
ALL_CAPS = re.compile(r"[A-Z]+")


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    """Activation at the current token. carry is unused: each prediction depends only on
    whether this token opens a document and what the token looks like."""
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    starts_document = prefix.position == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    if not starts_document:
        return None, 0.0
    if I_LOOKALIKE.fullmatch(token):
        return None, 1.0
    if token.startswith("\t"):
        return None, -0.5
    if LOWER_START.fullmatch(token) or not token.isascii():
        return None, -0.25
    if ALL_CAPS.fullmatch(token):
        return None, 0.2
    return None, 0.0

"""A sparse dictionary-based approximation to noun-ending activations.

On standalone Chinese-character suffix tokens, CC-CEDICT glosses suggest
formal human roles, commercial parties, organizations and event dates.
Those get positive values; ordinary person endings and recognized rooms
get small negatives, as do English '-ist' specialist glosses before 家.
Separate formatting rules cover initial Title: fields, initial chat openers
and repeated middle dots. Other positions are zero. State resets by document.
This explains only part of the observed activation, not its full computation.
"""
import re
from functools import lru_cache
import cedict

READS = ()

# English descriptions of legal, administrative and commercial capacities.
ROLE = re.compile(
    r'\b(supervisor|manager|administrator|representative|insurer|investor|'
    r'debtor|creditor|guardian|producer|heir|successor|recipient|sender|'
    r'consignee|mortgagor|trustee|guarantor|bidder|applicant|contractor|'
    r'owner|beneficiary|nominee|spokesperson|lecturer|speaker|agent)\b|'
    r'(natural|legal|contact) person')
CAPACITY = re.compile(
    r'payment|property right|mortgage|insurance|debt|invest|borrow|lend|'
    r'procure|purchase|inherit|pass on|pension|lecture|to draft')
COMMERCE = re.compile(
    r'business|trad(e|ing)|export|import|distribut|supply|retail|sell|'
    r'exhibit|endorse|franchise|contractor|dealer|merchant')
PARTY = re.compile(
    r'to receive|to transmit|to dispatch|to organize|to host|to hold|'
    r'to repair|maintenance|to supply|to provide|to deliver|receiving party')
EVENT = re.compile(
    r'register|settle|issu(e|ance)|releas|sell|sale|launch|expir|'
    r'delivery|maturity|deadline|benchmark')


@lru_cache(maxsize=8192)
def meanings(text):
    return ' ; '.join(cedict.glosses(text)).lower()


@lru_cache(maxsize=8192)
def noun_ending(left, token):
    """Look for a dictionary word at the right edge, not anywhere in the row."""
    ending = '人' if token == '人的' else token
    stems = [left[-n:] for n in range(1, min(6, len(left)) + 1)]
    compound = ' ; '.join(meanings(stem + ending) for stem in stems)
    stem_gloss = ' ; '.join(meanings(stem) for stem in stems if len(stem) >= 2)
    if ending == '人':
        if ROLE.search(compound) or CAPACITY.search(stem_gloss):
            return 'role', 2.3
        return 'ordinary_person', -0.15 if token == '人' else -0.23
    if ending == '方' and PARTY.search(stem_gloss + compound):
        return 'party', 0.8
    if ending == '商' and COMMERCE.search(stem_gloss + compound):
        return 'merchant', 0.6
    if ending in ('单位', '單位') and (
            PARTY.search(stem_gloss) or re.search(r'enroll|excavate|insure', stem_gloss)):
        return 'organization', 1.5
    if ending == '日' and EVENT.search(stem_gloss):
        return 'event_date', 1.2
    if ending == '室' and re.search(r'\b(room|office|laboratory)\b', compound):
        return 'room', -0.27
    if ending == '家' and re.search(r'\b\w+ist\b', compound):
        return 'specialist', -0.16
    return '', 0.0


ENDINGS = {'人', '人的', '方', '商', '日', '室', '家', '单位', '單位'}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        carry = (doc, 0, '', b'')
    _, position, previous, recent = carry
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    value = 0.0
    if token in ENDINGS:
        left = recent.decode('utf-8', errors='ignore')
        _, value = noun_ending(left, token)
    if position == 1 and previous == 'Title' and token == ':':
        value = 4.53
    if token == 'Title' and position == 0:
        value = -0.275
    if token == '<|im_start|>' and position == 0:
        value = 0.333
    if token and set(token) == {'·'} and previous and set(previous) == {'·'}:
        value = 0.438
    recent = (recent + prefix.token_bytes[-1])[-48:]
    return (doc, position + 1, token, recent), value

"""Layer-1 MLP down-projection, component 5535: a party-and-role noun detector.

In plain terms: this component is nearly silent most of the time (typical size about 0.04,
with a sign that simple rules cannot predict), so the program predicts 0 there. It responds
in three recognisable situations:

1. Role nouns ending in 人 ("person") in legal, financial and administrative text, e.g.
   受托人 (trustee), 管理人 (administrator), 自然人 (natural person), 发件人 (sender),
   被告人 (defendant), 借款人 (borrower), 投资人 (investor), 负责人 (person in charge).
   Their 人 is strongly positive (about +2.5). The 人 of ordinary "people" words
   (人们, 人生, 人口, ...) and other 人 uses is slightly negative (about -0.25).
   Other party and entity nouns are mildly positive: 单位, 所有人, 各方, 商, and
   方 after 发送, 接收, 管理 and similar.
2. The first token of each document (the row's first token, or the first token after
   <|endoftext|>). Code and markup openers (#, package, import, ')', <|im_start|>) are mildly
   positive; sentence openers such as "The", "I" and single capital letters are negative.
3. The "Title:" header that opens a document (<|endoftext|>Title:): the largest response,
   about +4.5. A run of middle dots (··) gives a steady +0.44.

The values are typical activations measured on training rows, rounded.
"""

READS = ()

# Legal, financial and administrative role stems that take the suffix 人.
PARTY_STEMS = (
    "托", "件", "自然", "管理", "訴", "告", "联系", "投诉", "法定代表", "占用",
    "投资", "投資", "保险", "保險", "债务", "債務", "借", "利", "当事", "监护",
    "監護", "产权", "產權", "讲", "创建", "创作", "犯罪嫌疑", "被", "负责", "負責",
    "纳税", "納稅", "参保", "參保", "收款", "义务", "義務", "著作权", "經紀", "经纪",
    "制片", "愿", "願", "经营", "經營", "申请", "申請", "发", "發", "代表",
)
# Ordinary "people" words whose 人 is not a role noun.
GENERAL_PEOPLE = (
    "人们", "人生", "人口", "人群", "人的", "人都", "每个人", "人心", "人物", "人间",
    "人們", "没有人", "人在",
)
# Party and entity nouns, with typical activations.
PARTY_NOUNS = {"单位": 1.0, "單位": 1.0, "所有人": 2.0, "各方": 0.8, "商": 0.4}
# 方 counts as a party noun only after these words.
PARTY_AFTER = {
    "方": ("发送", "接收", "经营管理", "管理", "举办", "投资", "维修", "收", "理"),
}
# Values for the first token of a document.
OPENER_POSITIVE = (
    "#", "package", "#include", "import", ")", "<|im_start|>",
    " {\n", "theorem", "//",
)
OPENER_NEGATIVE = (
    "The", " The", "I", "T", "S", "Q", "O", "W", "H", "K",
    "\n\n", "#!/", "int", "//\n", "\r",
)

    toks = prefix.token_strings
    tok = toks[-1]
    prev = toks[-2] if len(toks) > 1 else "<|endoftext|>"
    prev2 = toks[-3] if len(toks) > 2 else ""
    # A document starts at the row's first token and wherever document_ids changes.
    docs = prefix.document_ids
    doc_start = len(docs) == 1 or docs[-1] != docs[-2]

    if tok == ":" and prev == "Title" and prev2 == "<|endoftext|>":
        return None, 4.5
    if tok == "··":
        return None, 0.44
    if tok == "人":
        return None, (2.5 if prev in PARTY_STEMS else -0.25)
    if tok in GENERAL_PEOPLE:
        return None, -0.25
    if tok in PARTY_NOUNS:
        return None, PARTY_NOUNS[tok]
    if tok in PARTY_AFTER and prev in PARTY_AFTER[tok]:
        return None, 0.8
    if doc_start:
        if tok in OPENER_POSITIVE:
            return None, 0.3
        if tok in OPENER_NEGATIVE:
            return None, -0.4
    return None, 0.0

"""Layer 1, MLP down_proj, component 5537: a source-code declaration detector.

What it does: this component writes a positive push when the text is opening a
declaration in source code (a C/C++ header guard, a Java/C# `class` or `public`
member, a C# `/// <summary>` tag, a `/**` doc comment), once code-file scaffolding
(import / using / package / namespace / #include / #define) has already appeared.
It is negative on `[#permalink]` link anchors, on Java `import` lines, and on
`#include`. A repeated run of the middle-dot filler token '··' sits at about -2.

Main program: `step` keeps the last 60 tokens as text. For each token it looks up a
value in two tables. The keyword table is gated by whether code-file scaffolding
appears in that recent text. The rest is context-free. Predictions are zero
everywhere else.
"""
READS = ()

# Words that mark the text so far as a source-code file.
CODE_SCAFFOLD = ("import ", "using ", "package ", "namespace ", "#include", "#ifndef", "#define")

# Declaration openers: active only inside a code file (after scaffolding).
DECLARATION = {
    " class": 2.4,   # `public class Foo` inside a file
    "class": 0.8,
    "public": 1.6,   # `public` at the start of a line (member or class modifier)
    " public": 0.3,
    "#define": 2.1,  # header-guard `#define` after `#ifndef`
    "summary": 2.6,  # C# `/// <summary>`
    "/**\n": 2.0,    # Javadoc start
    " interface": 0.7,
    " //": 0.2,
    ' "': 0.3,
    "import": -0.3,  # Java import lines are mildly negative
    " import": -0.2,
    "#include": -0.15,
}

# Context-free features.
ANYWHERE = {
    "#ifndef": 7.0,  # header guard opener, strong anywhere
    "summary": 1.3,
    " fn": 0.7,      # Rust `fn`
    "/env": 2.0,     # `#!/usr/bin/env` shebang
    "php": 0.4,
    " parameter": -0.2,
}

def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    recent = carry or ()
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    prev = prefix.token_strings[-2] if len(prefix.token_strings) > 1 else ""
    text = "".join(recent)
    value = ANYWHERE.get(tok, 0.0)
    if tok in DECLARATION and any(word in text for word in CODE_SCAFFOLD):
        value = DECLARATION[tok]
    if tok == "permalink" and prev.endswith("[#"):
        value = -6.0     # `[#permalink]` anchor text
    if tok == "··" and prev == "··":
        value = -2.0     # a run of the repeated filler token
    return (recent + (tok,))[-60:], value

"""Document-start detector for layer 1's MLP output unit 5538.

What it does: this component writes a large value into the residual stream at the
first token of each document (and at a row's first token), and nowhere else. Its size
depends on which token it is: a whole word scores higher than punctuation, digits or
Chinese characters. The value is a fixed function of the token itself, because the
first token can only attend to itself.

It also stays on through a run of the same token that began the document (for
example "0 0 0 0"), since such a run also gives the attention nothing but copies of
that token. Any other later token gets 0.

Read it as: "fire at the start of a document, strength set by how word-like the
first token is, and keep firing while the document is only repeats of that token."
"""

READS = ()


def _is_cjk(text):
    return any("一" <= c <= "鿿" for c in text)


def start_value(text):
    """Predicted activation for a document's first token, from its decoded text."""
    core = text.strip()
    if not core:
        return 2.0
    value = 5.3 + 0.28 * min(len(core), 8)  # longer tokens (whole words) score higher
    if _is_cjk(text):
        value -= 1.5
    if core.isdigit():
        value -= 1.2
    elif not any(c.isalnum() for c in core):
        value -= 2.1                         # bare punctuation
    return value


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_ids[-1]
    text = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    new_doc = len(prefix) == 1 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    if new_doc or carry is None:
        start_token, start_text, repeats = token, text, True
    else:
        start_token, start_text, repeats = carry
        repeats = repeats and token == start_token
    carry = (start_token, start_text, repeats)
    return carry, (start_value(start_text) if repeats else 0.0)

"""Russian "to lead / conduct" roots, read off the text.

What the component does: it fires on the pieces of Russian words built on the
root вод- / вед- / вож- ("lead, conduct, guide") when a prefix comes before the
root: ввод (input), вывод (output), провод (wire), привод (drive), перевод
(translation), проведение, введение, сопровождение. The bare root syllable
(вод, вед, од, ед, ож) fires hardest; the endings that follow it inside the same
word fire weakly. The same meaning shows up in a few other places: 導 (Japanese /

величина, and the Latin-script pieces vod, ved, odes (Polish / Czech "lead",
as in voivodeship).

opens the word rather than sitting after a prefix, and words that merely contain
the letters (поведение, справедливо, производитель), where the model reacts
little.

Values are fitted means on training rows: 6 on the bare root syllable, 3 on a
piece that overlaps the root and adds letters, 1 on a later piece of the same
word, 4 on вели, 2 on 導 and on the Latin pieces, zero elsewhere.

import regex

ROOTS = ("вод", "вед", "вож")  # Cyrillic roots: lead, conduct, guide
BARE = ("од", "ед", "ож", "вод", "вед", "вел", "ел")  # the root syllable on its own
WORD = regex.compile(r"[\p{Cyrillic}\p{Latin}]")  # characters that belong to a word

BARE_VALUE = 6.0
PART_VALUE = 3.0
AFTER_VALUE = 1.0
VELI_VALUE = 4.0
HAN_VALUE = 2.0
LATIN_VALUE = 2.0

    # carry: (bytes of the current word so far, activation at the previous token)
    if len(prefix.token_ids) < 2 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]:

    tb = prefix.token_bytes[-1]
    text = tb.decode("utf-8", "replace")

    breaks = [i for i, ch in enumerate(text) if ch != "�" and not WORD.match(ch)]

        prev_value = 0.0

    w = word.decode("utf-8", "replace").lower()
    n_before = len(before.decode("utf-8", "replace"))

    value = 0.0
    for root in ROOTS:

        i = w.find(root, 1)

        value = AFTER_VALUE  # the ending of a word whose root just fired

        value = LATIN_VALUE

        value = HAN_VALUE
    return (word, value), value

- Fires on the word pieces "ied" and "led" when they sit inside a word of a non-English
  text (e.g. Italian "rich|ied|ere", Czech "pos|led|ního"): +2.0 for "ied", +1.0 for

  (+0.8 / +0.4) when there are a few; nothing when the context is clearly English.
- Everything else predicts 0. The component's activation is mostly near zero, so this is
  a sparse, mostly-silent prediction.

concepts that carry signal (the /testbed "bed" and the foreign "ied/led" pieces).

ENGLISH = set(
    "the of and to in a is was that for with on as by it he she his her this are be from "
    "at an or not which have has had were but they their there been will would can i you we".split()
)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip()
    if tok == "bed":

        if english < 0.15:

    return None, 0.0

irregular plural possessives, are negative. These are lexical and short-range
grammatical rules, not a complete parser; ambiguous and split words remain hard.

        support education training experience progress learning violence
        abuse fraud hate joy hope talent criticism competition caution
        scrutiny legislation terminology variability terror laughter
        nonsense silence justice freedom authority permission commerce

)

             'specific': -.33, 'respective': -.33}

SINGULAR = set('a an each every one'.split())

    among against without across between upon within about around toward towards'''.split())
PREDICATES = set('''am is are was were be been being seem seems seemed become
    becomes became feel feels look looks very quite entirely completely totally'''.split())
COUNT_CODES = set('''status error identification verification postal zip access
    area country security numeric coupon bar barcode'''.split())
COMPOSITION = set('water fat sugar salt protein carbon moisture alcohol'.split())
VERB_CUES = set('i we you they he she it will can could would should may might must to'.split())

    return wordnet.parts_of_speech(word)


@lru_cache(maxsize=20000)

    return bool(word.isalpha() and not word.endswith('s')

    for token in reversed(previous):

        if w in PREPOSITIONS or w in ('and', 'or'):

        if any(c in token for c in ',.;:!?\n'):

    return 0

    if w == 's' and p in ("'", '’') and len(previous) > 1:

        verb_use = 'verb' in parts(w) and p in VERB_CUES
        if count_code or measured_content or verb_use:
            value *= .3

            value *= .22

            value *= .6
        elif det == 2:
            value *= .9
        elif p == 'of' or 'adjective' in parts(p):
            value *= 1.9
        elif p in PREPOSITIONS:
            value *= 1.6
        elif 'verb' in parts(p):
            value *= 1.4
        elif not p or not any(c.isalpha() for c in p):
            value *= .6

    if token.strip()[:1].isupper():

    return value

    document = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    previous = () if carry is None or carry[0] != document else carry[1]
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    value = predict(token, previous)
    return (document, (*previous[-3:], token)), float(value)

    close equivalents "upon", "sur", "på", "auf", "par", ...) when they introduce an
    adjunct of place, time, event or agent: "played on", "educated at", "published by",

        where it is a required complement rather than an adjunct;

      - the filler token "··" that pads unused rows gets a negative value.

    before = last_word(text[: len(text) - len(word)].rstrip())  # the word before it

    value = computing_word_value(word)

        elif word == "with" and before == "up":

Two readable triggers:

1. The colon of a document that opens with "Title:", i.e. the text
   "<|endoftext|>Title:". It gives a large, fixed activation (about 6.6). This one
   case carries nearly all of the component's effect on the model.
2. The first token of a document. Positions restart at each document, so that token
   sees only itself and its activation depends on the token alone. Control-like tokens
   (tab, NUL, end-of-text) are clearly positive (about 1); capitalised words are
   mildly positive (0.16); code-like fragments starting with "_" or "." are mildly
   negative (-0.16); other tokens sit just above zero (0.06).

token identity, spread over thousands of tokens) and has no simple character-level
pattern, so it is not modelled here.
"""

READS = ()

TITLE_COLON = 6.6
CONTROL_TOKENS = {"\t", "\\t", "\x00", "<|endoftext|>"}


def _is_document_start(prefix):
    return prefix.position == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]


def _document_start_value(token):
    if token in CONTROL_TOKENS:
        return 1.0
    if token[:1] in ("_", "."):
        return -0.16
    if token.lstrip(" ")[:1].isupper():
        return 0.16
    return 0.06


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    s = prefix.token_strings
    if len(s) >= 3 and s[-3] == "<|endoftext|>" and s[-2] == "Title" and s[-1] == ":":
        return carry, TITLE_COLON
    if _is_document_start(prefix):
        return carry, _document_start_value(s[-1])
    return carry, 0.0
