"""Layer 1, MLP down-projection component 5547: the "IS" of a split acronym.

What it responds to, in plain terms:
- The token "IS" written right after one of a few short capital-letter
  pieces, so that the two together spell a known acronym or name that the
  tokenizer split in two: "OE|IS" (OEIS, the Online Encyclopedia of Integer
  Sequences), "I|IS" (IIS, Internet Information Services), "E|IS|PACK"
  (EISPACK), "BE|IS" (BEIS), "SE|IS". The component goes negative there, most
  strongly for OEIS. Other capital pieces before IS (NS, FS, PR, CHR, ...) give
  almost nothing, so they are left at zero.
- Everything else is zero. The rest of its activation is small, token-specific
  noise, and the first token of each document, which has no context to draw on.

`carry` is the run of capital letters that ends the text so far in the current
document; it is reset at each document boundary.
"""

import re

READS = ()

# capital-letter piece before "IS" -> activation (typical values seen in training data)
ACRONYM_PIECE = {"OE": -8.0, "E": -3.0, "BE": -2.9, "SE": -2.2, "I": -1.8}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    new_doc = len(prefix) == 1 or prefix.document_ids[-2] != prefix.document_ids[-1]
    run = "" if new_doc or carry is None else carry

    value = 0.0
    if tok == "IS":
        value = ACRONYM_PIECE.get(run, 0.0)

    m = re.search(r"[A-Z]+$", tok)
    run = run + tok if tok.isupper() and tok.isalpha() else (m.group(0) if m else "")
    return run, float(value)

"""Third digit of a year (layers.1.mlp.down_proj, unit 5548).

What it does: this unit is nearly silent everywhere except on the THIRD digit of a
number, the decade digit of a year-like number. For "1985" it fires on the "8"; for
"2004" on the "0". Digits in Qwen are single tokens, so the program tracks the run of
digits just before the current token (reset at each document start) and, when exactly
two digits came before, scores the current digit by those two leading digits:

- "19" (1900s): strongest, rising with the digit (about 1.3 for 190x up to 3.8 for 199x).
- "20" (2000s): 2.9 for 200x, 1.8 for 201x, about 0.9 for later decades.
- Other years 1300-2999 are moderate (about 0.6-1.2); 10xx about 0.5; 11xx 0.15,
  12xx 0.35; 00xx about 0; numbers starting with 3-9 get a small default of 0.4.
- Any other digit, or a digit that is not the third of a run, gives 0.

Why: the unit's job looks like marking "this is the decade of a year" so later
layers can predict the rest of the year. Non-digit tokens carry most of the remaining
variance and are not captured here.

Main program: step() keeps the digit run in the carry, then applies the rule above.
"""

READS = ()

DIGITS = set("0123456789")

# Activation on the third digit of a number, by the number's first two digits.
START = {"19": 2.9, "20": 2.0, "18": 1.2, "17": 1.1, "16": 1.1, "15": 1.1,
         "14": 0.9, "13": 0.7, "12": 0.35, "11": 0.15, "10": 0.5, "00": 0.05,
         "21": 0.6, "22": 0.9, "23": 1.0, "24": 0.8, "25": 1.0, "26": 0.95,
         "27": 0.75, "28": 0.7, "29": 0.65}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    run = carry or ""
    if prefix.position == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]:
        run = ""
    value = 0.0
    if len(token) == 1 and token in DIGITS:
        if len(run) == 2:
            value = START.get(run, 0.4)
            if run == "19":
                value = 1.3 + 0.28 * int(token)
            elif run == "20":
                value = {"0": 2.9, "1": 1.8}.get(token, 0.9)
        return run + token, value
    return "", value

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:5550, a weak, token-driven feature.

What it does, in plain terms:
- Chinese words of diligence, bravery, skill and goodness (勤, 善, 猛, 巧, 廉, 妙, 奇, 勇, 敢,
  勤奋, 勇敢, 巧妙, 廉洁 ...) push it clearly negative. 勤 is the strongest.
- Chinese words of abundance and ease (万 / 萬, 千万, 百万, 无限, 轻松, 美好, 良好, 欢迎,
  温暖, 温柔, 便利 ...) push it mildly positive.
- At the first token of a document (no context before it), code/markup openers and digits
  (#, import, package, theorem, /*, 0-9) push it mildly negative.
- Everywhere else it predicts 0.

The activation is mostly unexplained by any concept: most of its variance comes from
document-initial tokens and from many individual tokens with no shared meaning, which
this program does not capture.
"""

READS = ()

# Negative: praiseworthy traits and skills, written as the words themselves.
TRAIT = {
    "勤", "勇", "巧", "善", "奇", "猛", "妙", "廉", "敢", "洁", "忠",
    "英勇", "大胆", "勇敢", "勤奋", "巧妙", "廉洁", "奇妙",
}
# Positive: abundance (ten-thousand, million) and pleasant, easy, good-state words.
PLEASANT = {
    "万", "萬", "百万", "千万", "无限", "轻松", "美好", "良好", "良好的", "欢迎",
    "温暖", "温柔", "便利", "丰富的", "简单的",
}
# Document-initial code/markup openers.
CODE_START = {"#", "##", "import", "package", "theorem", "/*", "int", "from", "const", "#include"}

TRAIT_VALUE = -1.5
PLEASANT_VALUE = 0.6
CODE_START_VALUE = -0.4


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip()
    first = prefix.position == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    if first and (token.isdigit() or token in CODE_START):
        return None, CODE_START_VALUE
    if token in TRAIT:
        return None, TRAIT_VALUE
    if token in PLEASANT:
        return None, PLEASANT_VALUE
    return None, 0.0

"""Fires on the last digit of a year (1500-2099), e.g. the "4" in "1984", and more weakly on
the last digit of a thousands group in a comma-separated number, e.g. the "0" in "2,000".

Qwen writes numbers one digit per token, so the component sees each digit as it is typed.
Its contribution is large when the current digit is the fourth digit of a plain run of
digits that starts "19" or "20" (a year such as 1984, 2012 or 1905): about +3.5. Years
starting "18" give about +1.7, "17" about +0.8, "15"-"16" about +0.4. Other four-digit
numbers (10xx, 21xx, 0xxx) give nothing.

The last digit of a three-digit group after a comma (the final "0" in "2,000" or "1,172,000")
gives about +1.2. Everything else predicts 0. Digits must belong to the same
document as the current token; a new document resets everything.
"""

READS = ()

# Activation for a year, by its first two digits.
YEAR_SIZE = {"19": 3.5, "20": 3.5, "18": 1.7, "17": 0.8, "16": 0.5, "15": 0.3}
THOUSANDS_SIZE = 1.2


def is_digit(token):
    return len(token) == 1 and token in "0123456789"


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    s = prefix.token_strings
    docs = prefix.document_ids
    t = prefix.position
    value = 0.0
    # Year: the current token and the three before it are digits of one document,
    # and the run starts here (no digit before it).
    if t >= 3 and all(is_digit(s[i]) and docs[i] == docs[t] for i in range(t - 3, t + 1)):
        starts_run = t == 3 or not is_digit(s[t - 4]) or docs[t - 4] != docs[t]
        if starts_run:
            value = YEAR_SIZE.get(s[t - 3] + s[t - 2], 0.0)
    # Thousands group: ",ddd" with a digit before the comma, current token the last digit.
    if t >= 4 and all(is_digit(s[i]) for i in (t - 2, t - 1, t)):
        if s[t - 3] == "," and is_digit(s[t - 4]) and docs[t - 4] == docs[t]:
            value = max(value, THOUSANDS_SIZE)
    return carry, float(value)


def main():
    """Print where the program fires on a sample sentence, one character per token
    (Qwen also gives each digit its own token)."""
    class Prefix:
        pass

    tokens = list("Founded in 1984, it sold 2,000 units; rebuilt in 1792 and again in 2012.")
    carry = None
    for t in range(len(tokens)):
        prefix = Prefix()
        prefix.token_strings = tokens[: t + 1]
        prefix.document_ids = [0] * (t + 1)
        prefix.position = t
        carry, value = step(carry, prefix, {})
        if value:
            print(f"{tokens[t]!r} at {t}: {value}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""A local arithmetic-and-quantity detector.

The main response is positive on '=' after a numerical calculation, especially
near a document's start. Smaller rules recognize lengths, durations, geometric
locations, and selected mathematical symbols. Mathematical f and cos have
negative responses. Alphabetic first tokens get a small negative correction;
most other tokens receive a near-zero prediction. This is a partial fit.
"""
import re

READS = ()

LENGTH_UNITS = set('''mm cm km metre meter millimeter centimeter
    kilometer'''.split())
TIME_UNITS = set('second minute hour day week month year'.split())
MATH = re.compile(
    r'[=+*^λθπ]|\\(?:frac|sqrt)|\b(?:sin|cos|tan|function|equation)\b')
CODE = re.compile(
    r'\b(?:def|return|import|const|let|var|int|float|double|void)\b|[_;]')
GEOMETRY = re.compile(
    r'\b(?:points?|centroid|origin|radius|circle|line|midpoint|coordinates?'
    r'|located|angle)\b')
NUMBER_END = re.compile(r'[0-9]\s*$')
NUMBER_TAIL = re.compile(r'[0-9.\s+*/×÷−^()=-]+$')
CALCULATION = re.compile(
    r'[0-9][0-9.\s]*[+*/×÷−-]\s*[-+]?\s*[0-9]')


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        tail, position = '', 0
    else:
        _, tail, position = carry
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = token.strip()
    unit = word.removesuffix('s')  # Regular plurals of these unit names.
    numeric = bool(NUMBER_END.search(tail))
    mathematical = bool(MATH.search(tail))
    strong_math = (mathematical and not CODE.search(tail)
                   and sum(ch.isdecimal() for ch in tail) >= 3)
    value = -0.0015

    if position == 0 and word.isalpha():
        value -= 0.0855
    if word == '=' and numeric:
        expression = NUMBER_TAIL.search(tail)
        if expression and CALCULATION.search(expression.group()):
            value += 0.777
        if strong_math:
            value += 0.236
        if position < 8:
            value += 1.325
    elif word == '≈':
        value += 0.55
    elif word == 't' and strong_math:
        value += 0.26
    elif word == 'f' and strong_math and token.startswith(' '):
        value -= 0.356
    elif word == 'cos' and mathematical:
        value -= 0.209
    elif word == 'at' and token.startswith(' '):
        if GEOMETRY.search(tail[-90:]):
            value += 0.351
    elif unit in LENGTH_UNITS and numeric:
        value += 0.199
    elif unit in TIME_UNITS and numeric:
        value += 0.114
    elif word == 'π':
        value += 0.16
    elif word in {'θ', 'theta'} and re.search(r'(?:sin|cos|tan)\s*$', tail):
        value += 0.46

    return (doc, (tail + token)[-180:], position + 1), value

"""Approximate the component as a negative letter-P spelling signal.

Short P-bearing pieces receive larger negative values. Case, repeated P,
word endings, PH and complete angle-bracket tags adjust the response.
A little signal spills into the next token, more into continuing word
pieces; two-piece history is retained. Document starts, turn endings and
reasoning endings have separate offsets. This does not model lexical exceptions
or the component's irregular responses to long whitespace tokens.
"""
from functools import lru_cache
import math
import unicodedata
from anyascii import anyascii

READS = ()


@lru_cache(maxsize=32768)
def spelling(s):
    letters = ''.join(c for c in s.strip() if c.isalpha())
    n = max(1, len(letters))
    text = ''.join(
        anyascii(c) if any(script in unicodedata.name(c, '')
                           for script in ('LATIN', 'CYRILLIC', 'GREEK',
                                          'KATAKANA', 'HIRAGANA')) else c
        for c in letters
    ).lower()
    p = text.count('p')
    q = bool(p) / math.sqrt(n)
    arabic = ''.join(anyascii(c) for c in letters
                     if 'ARABIC' in unicodedata.name(c, ''))
    return text, letters.lower(), n, p, q, 'p' in arabic.lower()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    s = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    first = carry is None or carry[0] != doc
    _, previous, older, joined = (doc, 0., 0., False) if first else carry
    text, raw, n, p, q, arabic_p = spelling(s)
    has_p = bool(p)
    continuation = s[:1].isalpha()
    end_p = raw.endswith(('p', 'pe', 'ps', 'pes'))
    markup = s.startswith('<') and s.endswith('>')
    root = math.sqrt(n)
    # Current spelling: letter P, with a length-normalized magnitude.
    value = (
        -0.0163 - 2.0187 * q
        -0.2271 * text.startswith('p')
        -0.1378 * ('P' in s)
        -0.5871 * max(0, p - 1) / root
        -0.1086 * q * s.strip().isupper()
        +0.2610 * q * end_p * s[:1].isspace()
        +0.6591 * raw.count('ph') / root
        +0.5377 * has_p * markup
        -1.7381 * arabic_p
    )
    # Nearby P fragments spill over; adjacent P pieces get less overlap.
    value += previous * (0.9022 * has_p - 0.1911)
    if continuation:
        value -= previous * (0.8459 + 1.1717 / root)
        value -= 0.7445 * older * joined
    if first:
        value += 0.3412 + 1.7273 * has_p
    if s in ('<|im_end|>', '</think>'):
        value -= 0.9387
    return (doc, q, previous, continuation), float(value)

"""Explainer for layers.1.mlp.down_proj component 5554 (Qwen3-1.7B, layer 1 MLP).

What it does, in plain terms:
  * It responds to the word "edition" (and "Edition", "editions", "expedition") with a
    strong activation, about 4.5.
  * It responds to "addition"/"additions" with a strong activation, about 4 in most uses,
    but only about 1.8 in the stock phrase "In addition".
  * It responds more weakly to the word-ending piece "ition"/"itions" when a longer
    word is split so that "-ition" stands alone (e.g. "Invest|ition", "Add|ition"),
    about 1.5.
  * It is slightly positive on a colon right after a digit (clock times and scores such
    as "03:10"), about 0.3.
  * The first token of each document (position 0 of a row, or the first token after a
    document break) sits slightly negative, about -0.2.
  * Everything else is about zero. Words that only contain the letters, such as
    "condition", "position", "additional", "credit", "editor", stay at zero.

the current token, the one before it, and whether it starts a document, so it needs no
carry between positions.
"""

ADDITION_WORDS = {"addition", "additions"}
# Word-ending pieces "ition" / "itions" split off from a longer word.
ITION_PIECES = {"ition", "itions"}

    if len(prefix.document_ids) < 2:
        return True
    return prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]

    raw = prefix.token_strings[-1]

when the running text has just completed the letters "ko" (also "kō"), even
when the "k" and the "o" sit in different tokens ("Ko", "ko", "KO", "iko",

GERMAN_WORDS = frozenset(
    "der die das und ist nicht mit auf für ein eine einen sich von zu dem den des auch "
    "werden wird sie er es wir ich du ihr wie nach bei oder aber noch sein haben sind "
    "wurde wurden durch über".split()

their German, French and Portuguese counterparts) when the form is the auxiliary

before a past participle is due, so it tracks "a participle comes next" more than
any particular word.

  are and especially is only weakly, because "is" is usually copular ("this is",
  "the key is that").
- What comes before: after a personal pronoun or a clause word ("I was",
  "they are", "who is", "this is", "it is") the sentence is usually active or
  copular, so the value is cut to 0.3. After "may", "might" or "would" the next
  word is usually an adjective ("may be due to"), so it is 0. A being after is,
  are or was ("is being used") is the strongest passive cue, set to 2.5.

  pronouns (I, you, my, we, ...) in the previous 40 tokens of the same document,

    "was": 0.65, "were": 0.95, "been": 1.0, "being": 0.7,
    "be": 0.3, "is": 0.07, "are": 0.3,
    "wird": 0.6, "werden": 0.4, "wurde": 0.7, "wurden": 0.8,
    "être": 0.8, "été": 0.7, "sont": 0.3, "foi": 0.8,
}

# Words before a be-form that mark an active or copular clause.
NOT_A_THING = {
    "i", "he", "she", "we", "you", "they", "it", "this", "that", "which",
    "who", "what", "there", "here", "and",
}

# Modals that usually lead to an adjective, not a participle.
WEAK_MODALS = {"may", "might", "would"}

# Forms of "be" that make a following "being" a passive progressive.
BE_FORMS = {"is", "are", "was", "were", "be"}

# First- and second-person pronouns: the conversational register.
PERSONAL = {"i", "you", "my", "your", "me", "we", "our", "us"}

WINDOW = 40


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower()
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry["doc"] != doc:
        carry = {"recent": deque(maxlen=WINDOW), "doc": doc}
    value = STRENGTH.get(word, 0.0)
    if value and len(prefix.token_strings) > 1:
        before = prefix.token_strings[-2].strip().lower()
        if word == "being" and before in BE_FORMS:
            value = 2.5
        elif before in NOT_A_THING:
            value *= 0.3
        elif before in WEAK_MODALS:
            value = 0.0
    if value:
        personal = sum(carry["recent"])
        value *= max(0.0, 1.0 - 0.2 * personal)
    carry["recent"].append(1 if word in PERSONAL else 0)
    return carry, float(value)

    value += -1.22 * (split_ov)
    value += -3.01 * (split_ov and straddles('lov'))
    value += -1.48 * (split_ov and straddles('rov'))
    value += 2.45 * (split_ov and straddles('prov'))
    value += -1.24 * (straddles('lov') and not split_ov)
    value += -0.56 * (straddles('rov') and not split_ov)

    value += -0.41 * (contains('rov') and small)
    value += 0.56 * (contains('prov') and small)
    value += -1.82 * (love_form)
    value += -0.69 * (love_form and any(c.isupper() for c in current))
    value += 1.27 * (love_form and bare.endswith('ed'))
    value += 0.77 * (love_form and verb_lead)

    value += -0.38 * (bare=='over')
    value += -0.60 * (bare=='over' and joined)
    value += -1.77 * (bare=='over' and joined and prior[-1:] in 'lrn')

    value += 2.49 * (short_omb and word.endswith('ombs'))
    value += 2.53 * (short_omb and contains('comb') and joined)

    value += 4.61 * (split_ock)

    value += 3.79 * (bool(re.search('occal$',word)))

    value += 0.81 * (straddles('obb') and small)

    value += 2.74 * (current=='ク' and previous.endswith('ン'))
    value += 3.22 * (current in {'ク','ック'} and previous.endswith('コ'))

    previous = carry[1] if carry and carry[0] == document else ""

spelling families. Its activation is:

- strongly positive on "comb"/"cock"/"bomb" pieces (comb, combe, omb, bomb, tomb, cock,

Each family's value is roughly the average activation of its pieces in the training text.

how the model computes it.

OVEN_ROVE = {"oven", "rove", "rover", "clover", "overs", "overt", "overts", "verts", "vine",

OVER = {"over", "ov", "ove", "cov", "rov", "oved", "ovar", "crossover", "turnover", "över"}

"""Plural noun endings, weakened by a nearby definite article.

A short character history joins split words. WordNet supplies English noun
inflections; rare unknown s-endings supply a weaker fallback. Longer plurals
are positive, but 'the' in the last three words usually suppresses them.
Plural cue words can override that suppression. Nonplural words immediately
after a plural cue can be negative. Punctuation resembling code weakens
long plurals. Short object nouns have a separate intermediate level.
These are approximate rules, not a full noun-phrase parser.
"""
import re
from functools import lru_cache
import wordnet
from wordfreq import zipf_frequency

READS = ()
FUNCTION_WORDS = set('''a an the as is was has does this his its us yes thus
always perhaps besides whereas plus versus towards sometimes
he she it you i we they me him her them our your their my mine
these those there here whose theirs ours yours hers'''.split())
PLURAL_CUES = set('''many several multiple various different few these
those some all both two three four five six seven eight nine ten'''.split())
MORE_PLURAL_CUES = PLURAL_CUES | {'other', 'numerous', 'countless'}
IRREGULAR_PLURALS = set('children men women feet teeth mice geese oxen'.split())


@lru_cache(maxsize=100000)
def number_properties(word):
    w = word.lower()
    if not w.isascii() or not w.isalpha() or w in FUNCTION_WORDS:
        return False, False, 0.0, False, 0
    bases = wordnet.base_forms(w, 'noun')
    plural = any(b != w for b in bases) and (
        w.endswith('s') or w in IRREGULAR_PLURALS)
    s_ending = w.endswith('s') and not w.endswith(
        ('ss', 'ous', 'us', 'is', 'ics'))
    artifact = 'noun.artifact' in wordnet.categories(w, 'noun')
    return plural, s_ending, zipf_frequency(w, 'en'), artifact, len(w)


def predict(token, history):
    text = history + token
    match = re.search(r'[A-Za-z]+$', text)
    active = bool(token and token[-1].isascii() and token[-1].isalpha())
    word = match.group() if match and active else ''
    preceding = text[:-len(word)] if word else text
    words = re.findall(r'[A-Za-z]+', preceding.lower())
    previous = re.findall(r'[A-Za-z]+|\d+', preceding.lower())
    previous = previous[-1] if previous else ''
    plural_cue = bool(set(words[-3:]) & MORE_PLURAL_CUES)
    code_prefix = bool(preceding and preceding[-1] in '._/"=')
    punctuation = bool(word and not token[0].isalpha()
                       and not token[0].isspace())
    plural, s_ending, frequency, artifact, length = number_properties(word)
    if plural:
        if 'the' in words[-3:]:
            if plural_cue:
                return 0.3445
            return -0.0328 if (words and words[-1] == 'the') else 0.0732
        if length <= 4:
            return 0.1812 if artifact else 0.0538
        return 0.0074 if code_prefix else 0.4281
    if s_ending:
        if frequency <= 2.5:
            return 0.2487 if word.islower() else 0.0967
        return -0.0125 if punctuation else 0.0355
    if previous in PLURAL_CUES:
        return -0.2046 if artifact else -0.0717
    return -0.0035


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    history = carry[1] if carry is not None and carry[0] == doc else ''
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    value = predict(token, history)
    return (doc, (history + token)[-80:]), value

the component's weak negative values on some singular nouns after modifiers are not modelled.

per-position predictions for a set of rows.

    "the", "a", "an", "this", "that", "these", "those",
    "his", "her", "their", "its", "my", "your", "our",
}
NOT_PLURAL = {
    "is", "was", "has", "does", "gets", "makes", "wants", "speaks", "exists", "allows",
    "includes", "returns", "comes", "says", "contains", "looks", "takes", "ends", "shows",
    "follows", "starts", "gives", "becomes", "goes", "seems", "needs", "means", "uses",
    "provides", "requires", "depends", "works", "lets", "runs", "holds", "keeps", "sets",
    "this", "his", "its", "hers", "ours", "yours", "always", "perhaps", "sometimes",
    "towards", "themselves", "us", "thus", "less", "unless", "plus", "yes", "news",
    "series", "bus", "gas", "status", "process", "class", "analysis", "basis",
}

PLURAL_VALUE = 0.4         # typical activation on a determiner-free plural noun


def _is_plural_noun(word):
    """A word that looks like a plural common noun: letters only, ending in -s."""
    return (
        word.isalpha()
        and len(word) >= 3
        and word.endswith("s")
        and not word.endswith(("ss", "us", "is"))
        and not word[0].isupper()
        and word.lower() not in NOT_PLURAL

        if not before.isalpha():

    return None, PLURAL_VALUE
